subject: Post-call: deployment constraints & SLO confirmation for SkyLumen

Subject: Post-call recap — deployment constraints & next steps

Hi Elena / SkyLumen team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — useful discussion and good alignment on priorities. Quick recap of what we heard from you and the immediate asks so we have a shared starting point: 

Pain points (as described):
- High tail latency on your current model serving for inference-heavy personalization, visibly impacting search relevance.
- Limited ops visibility: hard to map cost per feature and to debug KV-cache misses across user cohorts.
- Procurement timeline: procurement team needs an estimated SLO & capacity plan to start commercial review.

Goals you reiterated:
- Reduce P95 generation latency for recommendation responses to under ~150 ms for 256-token outputs.
- Operate on a predictable cost model (targeting a 30% reduction vs current infra spend for the same QPS).
- Maintain tenant isolation and attach audit logs for initial pilot.

Agreed next steps (we committed on call):
1) Redwood to share a short technical SLO / topology note showing two viable deployment modes (Hosted + Dedicated) and expected latency/throughput ranges. (owner: Karthik, ETA: 24 hours)
2) We’ll supply a 2-week test plan for pilot traffic shape so you can validate tail latency and cost. (owner: Jordan, ETA: next Wed)
3) SkyLumen to share sample QPS and typical prompt length distribution (you mentioned median prompt ~38 tokens).

Attached the slide-deck and a quick topology sketch we used in the call.

If I missed anything or you want different prioritization, flag it here and we’ll update. Otherwise we’ll follow up with the technical note and a proposed pilot checklist by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — that matches our notes. A couple clarifications from the eng team that will determine the topology you suggest: 

1) Traffic profile: baseline 75 QPS with 10% spikes up to 220 QPS during hourly bursts. Median response length ~45 tokens; tail (95th) ~250 tokens.
2) Latency target: our product goal is P95 < 150 ms end-to-end for a single-turn recommendation call (includes network + inference). We know network varies between regions.
3) Data controls: for the pilot we need audit logs and ability to disable long-term retention. SOC2 evidence will be requested later in procurement.

Could you confirm in the technical note: expected P95 numbers for both Hosted and Dedicated options given our profile, and an estimated monthly spend ballpark for pilot shape (we can share exact traffic later)? Also please call out any bounded risks for caching (prefetching) and model tail effects.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Elena
Director, Product — SkyLumen

Subject: RE: Post-call recap — deployment constraints & next steps (technical note)

Elena — thanks for the extra detail. Below is a compact technical readout that maps your traffic to two practical deployment options and the expected SLOs / cost levers. I kept it intentionally prescriptive so procurement has numbers to review.

Assumptions from your note: baseline 75 QPS, burst 220 QPS (10% sustained spikes), median tokens/request 45, p95 tokens ~250. Latency budget target is P95 < 150 ms end-to-end (network + compute). We’ll highlight cloud-region variance separately.

Option A — Redwood Hosted (multi-tenant with burst pool)
- Topology: request -> router -> multi-tenant serving pool (GPU-accelerated), KV prefix cache + request-level batching (dynamic). Fallback path to smaller quantized variant for capacity pressure.
- Expected latency (typical US region): p50 ~30–45 ms compute, p95 ~90–160 ms compute depending on output length; end-to-end P95 estimate including 20–30 ms network overhead: ~110–190 ms.
- Throughput: sustained per-GPU concurrency 180–250 tokens/sec (fp16 kernels) for LLM-7B variants; effective QPS supported depends on avg output token length. For your median 45 tokens/request, a single GPU can handle ~20–35 QPS depending on batching efficiency.
- Cost levers: batching window, KV caching TTL, and quantized fallback. Likely path to 25–40% cost reduction vs current unmanaged infra under typical prefixes if caching is effective.
- Risks / mitigations: tail latency during burst when batching increases; mitigation via (1) routing burst traffic to reserved warm instances, (2) adaptive batch-timeouts, (3) shadow routing to observe tail without impact.

Option B — Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, single-tenant)
- Topology: VPC peering or private link to dedicated GPU pool under your account, optional private control-plane. KV cache either colocated (preferred) or remote (higher latency). Canary bucket routing for pilot.
- Expected latency (typical US region): p50 ~25–35 ms compute, p95 ~70–120 ms compute; end-to-end P95 with network: ~100–140 ms. Narrower tail because no noisy neighbors and smaller quantization variance.
- Throughput: dedicated pools sized to match burst capacity. Example sizing for your peak 220 QPS and 45 tokens median: target ~8–12 GPUs (7B fp16 profile) with autoscale headroom, depending on desired p95 headroom and batch sizing.
- Cost profile: higher fixed commit cost but lower unit token cost at scale; good fit if you need predictable performance and isolation for audit/SOC requirements.

SLO suggestions (pilot-phase):
- P95 latency (end-to-end): target 140 ms (conservative) with escalation if observed > 160 ms for 5% of pilot window.
- Availability: 99.9% for inference endpoints during pilot window.
- Cache effectiveness: target > 40% prefix-hit rate for common recommendation patterns to realize cost improvements.

Pilot test plan items (high level):
1) Run 72-hour pilot with synthetic replay of your production distribution (we’ll accept trace or histogram).
2) Measure P50/P95/P99 compute latency and end-to-end RTT, KV hit rates, and cost per 1M tokens.
3) Observe tail behavior under 3x burst events and test fallback routing policies.

Immediate asks from SkyLumen to finalize numbers:
- Confirm sample trace (one-day CSV or histogram) or share a small synthetic generator.
- Confirm whether private peering is a hard requirement for the pilot or negotiable for Dedicated.

I'll attach a quick topology sketch and a cost sketch in the follow-up deck Jordan sent. If this aligns I can convert the sizing to a shortlist of exact GPU SKUs and an estimated monthly spend for pilot traffic.

—Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
